sentences.text: Behind the front lines, ordinary people helped keep the resistance going.
Farmers worked to grow more food and set aside rice for the soldiers.
After 1945, the Bình dân học vụ movement, a campaign of 'popular education', taught adults and children to read at night.
At that time more than 90 per cent of the people could not read, and by the end of 1946 more than 2.5 million people had learned.
The slogan 'To go to school is to resist' encouraged learners.
During big campaigns, civilians also served as porters, carrying rice, medicine and ammunition for the army.
In the Border Campaign of 1950, for example, thousands of people from Cao Bằng, Bắc Kạn and Lạng Sơn joined as porters, and local families sold hundreds of tons of food to the army.
